messages.content: You classify arguments. You answer with JSON only.

A debater was assigned to defend one of two responses to a question ("my response") and to argue against
the other ("the other response"). Read the debater's argument below and decide which of these it does:

- "defends": it argues that its own response is correct.
- "concedes": it says or clearly implies that the other response is correct, or that its own response is wrong.
- "unclear": it does neither clearly.

# Argument

My response is correct.

The Indonesian is even, so position 2. Since “the person who is indonesian is not anywhere to the left of the person who is malaysian,” Malaysian is position 1 and Egyptian is position 3. The premise “the person that watches thriller movies is not anywhere to the left of the person who is egyptian” then forces thriller to position 3. The ice-hockey person must be between snowboarding and thriller, so snowboarding is position 1, ice-hockey position 2, thriller position 3.

Time-travel has different parity from Indonesian (position 2), so time-travel is position 1 or 3; position 3 is already thriller, so time-travel is position 1. The last premise says time-travel either listens to jazz or is Indonesian, but not both. It is not Indonesian, so it listens to jazz.

Dubstep has the same parity as Egyptian (position 3, odd), so dubstep is position 1 or 3. But position 1 listens to jazz, so dubstep must be position 3. Position 3 watches thriller.

The other response wrongly assumes dubstep “can’t be in position 3 (Egyptian)” even though no premise says dubstep and Egyptian are distinct. It then puts dubstep at position 1, but position 1 is time-travel and must listen to jazz, contradicting dubstep. Therefore ***thriller*** is correct.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this format:
{"verdict": "<defends, concedes or unclear>"}
